name: Poop
lede: Poop is a murky yellow-brown, a blunt informal name that sits in our data from a 2010 online color survey.

sections.title: A name with no recorded origin
sections.body: The name is a modern, informal one, and in our records it comes from a 2010 color-naming survey, with no older source [1]. Nothing in the color books we hold records it as a color before that, so its origin is simply undocumented here [1].

sections.title: An older fashion for dirty yellow
sections.body:
The idea is older than the survey. Pastoureau recounts that in the last weeks of 1751 Paris and the court wore a brownish yellow called *caca-dauphin*, to celebrate the birth of Louis XV's first grandson [2]. The same author says the shade, which we would now call mustard, had been counted since the Middle Ages as the ugliest of all colors [2]. The fashion lasted only a few weeks, and the name sits in a list of lively eighteenth-century color names that also included Paris mud and the belly of a Carmelite [3].

For today's closest named relatives, see [[mustard]] and [[mustard-yellow]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive the swatch appears in 334 paintings, as photographed, more common than 67% of the named colors [1]. It peaks in the 1800s and is most often an accent [1]. As with any dull brown-yellow, varnish that has yellowed with age can drift a painting toward this color, so the match says little about the pigment [1].
